title: Attribution Lens — Per‑Route Cost Drift Inspector (UX Prototype)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype an Attribution Lens — a focused Console view that surfaces per-route and per-model cost drift over time, with interactive decomposition and exportable artifacts. This ticket covers the UX copy, wireframes, prototype links, and initial review notes for the first iteration. The feature helps platform and product engineers quickly surface anomalous cost increases, attribute them to model variants / prompt patterns / request routing, and export a trace for audit or billing reconciliation.
design_summary: Primary goals: 1) Make cost drift visible at route-level (small multiples + sparkline anomaly badges) 2) Provide fast root-cause slicing (model, quantization, batch, prefix cache hit/miss, token types) 3) Enable one-click trace export (CSV/JSON) for downstream billing or incident handoff. Core UI patterns: timeline slider to focus windows, progressive decomposition panel, role-aware toggles (dev vs finance), and inline suggestions for remediation (e.g., pin cheaper variant, enable prefix cache).
decisions: Show per-route small multiples (top 12 routes by spend) on page load to surface hotspots quickly.
Default time window = 14 days with fast presets (24h, 7d, 14d, 30d).
Anomaly detection is client-side thresholding at design time (visual flags only). Product will wire server-side anomaly signals later.
Export formats: CSV for finance, JSON trace for engineering replay. Include provenance metadata (model version, route id, request id samples).
Progressive disclosure: show aggregated cost bars by default; expand to token-level token-type breakdown on demand to avoid cognitive overload.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs clarity: Showing token-level breakdowns in-line makes cards dense; we chose expandable drilldowns to keep the overview scannable.
Performance: live decomposition for many routes is expensive. We will lazy-load detailed slices when users expand a route or adjust the slider.
Privacy: including request ids aids debugging but must honor PII/data policies. We will mask full payloads and include 'sampled request id' only with appropriate role permission.
usability_notes: Test with PMs and 3 engineering on-call users to validate that the anomaly badges correlate with real incidents.
Validate that export contains stable keys for join back to logs (route_id, model_version, timestamp window).
Onboarding micro-copy: 'How to use' tooltip outlining steps to go from hotspot -> slice -> export.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype exists in Figma with interactive timeline and expandable route cards.
Design review completed with Eng and PM; feedback items captured as separate sub-issues.
Export spec documented (CSV & JSON schema) and linked in PRD.
Accessibility check: color contrast for anomaly badges meets AA; keyboard navigation for slider and expand controls follows patterns.
Mock data demonstrates a clear cost drift case and a resolved remediated case for QA validation.
